statements.name: Spec
statements.says: The factory starts with no post on the issue, and every step is a Next step.

statements.name: TypeOK
statements.says: The issue's state is always one of the ten kinds of post, and everything else the factory knows has its expected type.

statements.name: OnlyDirectorsDirect
statements.says: Every command the factory acted on came from a person with write access, never from anyone else or from a bot.

statements.name: RatifiesCurrentProposal
statements.says: Whenever something is ratified, built or merged, it is the current proposal.

statements.name: NoOpenQuestionsWhenRatified
statements.says: Nothing is ratified while a question is still open.

statements.name: AmendsHeldLock
statements.says: A proposal is ratified only while the base branch holds the lock it amends.

statements.name: MergedGatePassed
statements.says: When the factory merges, CI's gate passed on the commit it merged.

statements.name: MergedCurrentHead
statements.says: When the factory merges, the commit it merged is the pull request's current head.

statements.name: MergedOneProject
statements.says: When the factory merges, the pull request changes only its one project.

statements.name: MergedLockRatified
statements.says: When the factory merges, the project's lock is exactly the ratified proposal.

statements.name: StopLimit
statements.says: At most two builds of an issue stop partway before a writer says retry.

statements.name: StoppedHasNoPullRequest
statements.says: When a build stops, or the factory refuses to start one, there is no pull request.

statements.name: BuildStartsClean
statements.says: When a ratified proposal waits for its build, nothing is left of an earlier pull request: no head, CI result, lock, scope or merge.

statements.name: RebuildsOwnFailures
statements.says: A retry retires a pull request to build its ratified proposal again only after the build failed its own gate in the factory's run, never after CI's gate failed or the pull request couldn't merge.

statements.name: QuestionsAsked
statements.says: The factory can ask questions.

statements.name: GotStuck
statements.says: The factory can get stuck.

statements.name: FoundUnsupported
statements.says: The factory can find an issue unsupported.

statements.name: PullRequestFailed
statements.says: A pull request can fail CI's gate.

statements.name: OthersClosed
statements.says: Someone else can close the pull request.

statements.name: OthersMerged
statements.says: Someone else can merge the pull request.

statements.name: FactoryMerges
statements.says: The factory can merge its pull request.

statements.name: AmendmentMerges
statements.says: The factory can merge an amendment to an existing lock.

statements.name: BuildStopped
statements.says: A build can stop before it makes a pull request, and the factory posts that it failed.

statements.name: BuildRefusedAtLimit
statements.says: After two builds of an issue stop partway, the factory can refuse to start a third and post that the build failed.

statements.name: OwnGateFailed
statements.says: When the code fails the gate in the factory's own run, the factory can open a draft pull request and post that the build failed.

statements.name: CannotMerge
statements.says: A pull request that passed CI's gate but changes more than its one project or has a lock other than the ratified proposal can fail.

statements.name: RebuiltAndMerged
statements.says: A writer's retry can build a build that failed its own gate again, and the factory can merge the new build's pull request.

statements.name: RebuiltAndStopped
statements.says: After a retry builds a failed build again, the new build can stop before it makes a pull request, and the factory posts that it failed.

statements.name: RebuiltFailedAgain
statements.says: The new build can fail its own gate again and leave another draft pull request, for another retry.

statements.name: ObeyAnyone
statements.says: A bot or someone without write access gets the factory to take the issue.

statements.name: RatifyEarlier
statements.says: A ratify naming an earlier proposal's hash is accepted.

statements.name: RatifyOverMovedLock
statements.says: An amendment is ratified after the base branch's lock has moved.

statements.name: MergeOnAnyPass
statements.says: The factory merges a commit that passed CI even though it is no longer the pull request's head.

statements.name: MergeIgnoringLock
statements.says: The factory merges without checking that the project's lock is the ratified proposal.

statements.name: StartPastLimit
statements.says: The factory starts a third build after two builds of the issue have stopped partway and no writer has said retry.

statements.name: MergeFailedBuild
statements.says: The factory merges a pull request whose build failed, before a writer says retry and CI's gate passes.

statements.name: RebuildKeepsDraft
statements.says: A retry builds a failed build again but keeps its draft's head, CI's result and lock for the next build.

statements.name: RebuildAfterCI
statements.says: A retry builds a pull request that failed CI's gate again, instead of watching it again.

statements.name: FollowupSourceAuthorized
statements.says: A decision follow-up is authorized only by the exact ratified plan in its merged source pull request and the decision that source still owes.

statements.name: FollowupAssociationAuthenticated
statements.says: A follow-up must match the independently verified association between its source obligation and its own pull-request identity, so a claimed source or matching branch cannot authorize another pull request.

statements.name: FollowupSourcePreserved
statements.says: Observing or processing a decision follow-up preserves the source issue’s ratified plan and merged history.

statements.name: FollowupStableIdentity
statements.says: An authorized follow-up keeps its own pull-request identity through every accepted step, including retries and resumes.

statements.name: FollowupNoNewRatification
statements.says: A decision follow-up neither ratifies a new plan nor fabricates a project lock.

statements.name: FollowupMergedCurrentHead
statements.says: When the factory merges a decision follow-up, it merges that follow-up’s current head.

statements.name: FollowupNarrowMerge
statements.says: A follow-up merge requires independently verified scope on its current head containing only decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md changes tied to its source obligation.

statements.name: FollowupCurrentDecisionChecks
statements.says: A follow-up merge requires successful current-head decision checks including the decision graph check, with the project gate either passed or intentionally skipped together with independently verified follow-up scope.

statements.name: FollowupTrustedBase
statements.says: The factory merges a decision follow-up only into a trusted base.

statements.name: FollowupCommandsAuthorized
statements.says: Only an authenticated person with repository write access, never a bot, may request a decision follow-up retry or resume.

statements.name: FollowupCoreAccepted
statements.says: Given an externally supplied acceptance receipt from the amended Workflow for the exact request context, every applied follow-up step preserves that context and its accepted before-state, after-state and effect outcome.

statements.name: FollowupHumanHold
statements.says: A closed follow-up retains its human hold, and only an accepted explicit resume can clear a hold before a merge.

statements.name: FollowupRetryRenewsAllowance
statements.says: An accepted retry of blocked follow-up work renews its repair allowance with no repairs used.

statements.name: FollowupClosedRetryResumes
statements.says: A retry of closed follow-up work is an explicit resume of the same existing pull request.

statements.name: FollowupTwoRepairsPerAllowance
statements.says: The amended Workflow’s repair count for a follow-up’s current allowance stays at most two.

statements.name: HumanMergedPlanFollowupMerges
statements.says: With the corresponding Workflow steps accepted, an eligible plan merged by a person with write access can lead to a follow-up merge.

statements.name: ClosedFollowupResumesSamePR
statements.says: With the corresponding Workflow resume accepted, a closed follow-up can resume under the same pull-request identity.

statements.name: SkippedProjectGateFollowupMerges
statements.says: A follow-up can merge after an intentional project-gate skip when its current decision checks and independent scope verification succeed.

statements.name: BlockedFollowupGetsNewAllowance
statements.says: With the corresponding Workflow retry accepted, a blocked follow-up can receive a renewed repair allowance.

statements.name: ClosedFollowupKeepsHold
statements.says: A follow-up can close while retaining its human hold.

statements.name: AcceptedEffectFailurePreserved
statements.says: The protocol can preserve a failed effect outcome accepted by the amended Workflow.

statements.name: FollowupOpenUnmergedSource
statements.says: The protocol opens a decision follow-up from a source that has not merged.

statements.name: FollowupOpenNonOwingSource
statements.says: The protocol opens a decision follow-up from a merged source that owes no decision.

statements.name: FollowupOpenForgedAssociation
statements.says: The protocol grants follow-up authority to a pull request with a forged source association.

statements.name: FollowupMergeBroaderScope
statements.says: The factory merges a follow-up without independently verifying its narrow scope on the current head.

statements.name: FollowupMergeStaleCI
statements.says: The factory merges a follow-up using successful decision checks from an earlier head.

statements.name: FollowupMergeOldHead
statements.says: The factory merges an earlier follow-up head despite acceptance and checks for the current head.

statements.name: FollowupRetryUnauthorized
statements.says: The protocol accepts a follow-up retry or resume from a bot, a non-writer or an unauthenticated requester.

statements.name: FollowupApplyStaleAcceptance
statements.says: The protocol applies Workflow acceptance for an earlier request context after the follow-up head has changed.

statements.name: FollowupMergeWithoutGraphCheck
statements.says: The factory treats an intentional project-gate skip as permission to merge despite a failed current decision graph check.

statements.name: FollowupResumeReplacesPR
statements.says: The protocol resumes a closed follow-up by replacing its pull request.

statements.name: FollowupChangesEffectOutcome
statements.says: The protocol changes the effect outcome of an accepted Workflow step.

proposal.module_text:
---- MODULE IssueProtocol ----
EXTENDS Naturals, FiniteSets, Sequences

CONSTANTS Actors, Writers, Bots, Questions, Proposals, Heads, NoP, NoHead, NoActor,
          PullRequests, SourcePR, FollowPR, NoPR, Decisions,
          WorkflowInitial, WorkflowViewRows, WorkflowStepRows, BaseRefs, TrustedBases,
          NoSource, NoPermit, NoAudit

VARIABLES state, open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
          head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
          stops, failure, rebuiltAfter,
          sourceActor, source, follow, permit, audit

ordinaryVars == <<state, open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
          head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
          stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

followVars == <<sourceActor, source, follow, permit, audit>>

vars == <<state, open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
          head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
          stops, failure, rebuiltAfter,
          sourceActor, source, follow, permit, audit>>

Kinds == {"none", "asked", "proposed", "stuck", "unsupported",
          "ratified", "pr_open", "failed", "merged", "closed"}

\* Why the issue's latest failure happened.
Failures == {"none", "stopped", "limit", "gate", "ci", "unmergeable"}

\* rebuiltAfter is the failure a writer's retry last built the ratified
\* proposal again after, while the factory's run of the new build is all
\* there is to see: drafting again, a push to the pull request or a move of
\* the base branch forgets it. Only RebuildsOwnFailures and the witnesses of
\* a rebuild read it, and forgetting it keeps the model from holding every
\* later state twice.

\* Builds of an issue that may stop partway before the factory refuses another.
MaxStops == 2

\* Only people with write access who are not bots direct the factory.
Directors == Writers \ Bots

Locks == Proposals \cup {NoP}

\* States in which a ratified proposal is being built or has been merged.
Building == {"ratified", "pr_open", "failed", "merged"}

FactoryMerged == state = "merged" /\ mergedBy = "factory"

\* The original issue variables continue to describe the ordinary source build.
\* Follow-up work has separate authority and never changes that history.
\* WorkflowSteps and WorkflowViews are an interface to the independently proved,
\* amended decision-followup.Workflow, not a replacement implementation of it.
\* A step is <<before token, operation, effect outcome, after token>>.
\* A view is <<token, phase, human hold, allowance token, repairs used>>.
\* The checking bounds supply small illustrative accepted paths. Production
\* acceptance must come from that Workflow for the entire matching context.

\* TLC config values support nested sets; these tagged rows encode tuples
\* without baking the external Workflow relation into pinned helper definitions.
RowField(row, tag) ==
    CHOOSE value \in ((CHOOSE field \in row : tag \in field) \ {tag}) : TRUE

RowRepairCount(value) ==
    CASE value = "0" -> 0
      [] value = "1" -> 1
      [] value = "2" -> 2
      [] OTHER -> 3

WorkflowViews ==
    {<<RowField(row, "tokenTag"), RowField(row, "phaseTag"),
       RowField(row, "holdTag") = "true", RowField(row, "allowanceTag"),
       RowRepairCount(RowField(row, "repairsTag"))>> : row \in WorkflowViewRows}

WorkflowSteps ==
    {<<RowField(row, "beforeTag"), RowField(row, "operationTag"),
       RowField(row, "outcomeTag"), RowField(row, "afterTag")>> : row \in WorkflowStepRows}

CoreStates == {v[1] : v \in WorkflowViews}

CoreView(c) == CHOOSE v \in WorkflowViews : v[1] = c

CorePhase(c) == CoreView(c)[2]

CoreHold(c) == CoreView(c)[3]

CoreAllowance(c) == CoreView(c)[4]

CoreRepairs(c) == CoreView(c)[5]

CoreOperations == {"open", "classify", "repair", "effect", "close", "retry", "resume", "merge"}

CoreOutcomes == {t[3] : t \in WorkflowSteps}

CoreTransitionType == CoreStates \X CoreOperations \X CoreOutcomes \X CoreStates

AllowedFollowupArtifacts == {"decisions/", "SPEC.md", "README.md"}

\* Artifact values denote path classes; decisions/ includes its descendants.
ArtifactClasses == AllowedFollowupArtifacts \cup {"project-code"}

FollowGateResults == {"none", "pass", "fail", "skip"}

SourceHistory ==
    [state |-> state, proposal |-> proposal, ratified |-> ratified,
     ratifiedBase |-> ratifiedBase, amends |-> amends, open |-> open,
     head |-> head, prLock |-> prLock, mergedBy |-> mergedBy,
     mergedHead |-> mergedHead, merger |-> sourceActor]

SourceHistoryType ==
    [state : Kinds, proposal : Locks, ratified : Locks, ratifiedBase : Locks,
     amends : Locks, open : SUBSET Questions, head : Heads \cup {NoHead},
     prLock : Locks, mergedBy : {"nobody", "factory", "other"},
     mergedHead : Heads \cup {NoHead}, merger : Actors \cup {NoActor}]

AuthorityType == Locks \X PullRequests \X Decisions

SourceType ==
    [history : SourceHistoryType, isPlan : BOOLEAN, owes : BOOLEAN,
     pr : PullRequests, decision : Decisions, claim : AuthorityType,
     candidatePR : PullRequests]

FollowType ==
    [pr : PullRequests \cup {NoPR}, head : Heads \cup {NoHead},
     ciHead : Heads \cup {NoHead}, gate : FollowGateResults,
     decisions : BOOLEAN, graph : BOOLEAN, scopeHead : Heads \cup {NoHead},
     paths : SUBSET ArtifactClasses, tied : BOOLEAN, target : BaseRefs,
     core : CoreStates, mergedHead : Heads \cup {NoHead},
     outcome : CoreOutcomes \cup {"none"}, resumed : BOOLEAN,
     planRatification : Locks, projectLock : Locks]

ContextType ==
    [authority : AuthorityType, sourcePR : PullRequests, pr : PullRequests,
     head : Heads \cup {NoHead}, core : CoreStates,
     actor : Actors \cup {NoActor}, authenticated : BOOLEAN,
     ci : (Heads \cup {NoHead}) \X FollowGateResults \X BOOLEAN \X BOOLEAN,
     scope : (Heads \cup {NoHead}) \X (SUBSET ArtifactClasses) \X BOOLEAN,
     target : BaseRefs]

PermitType == [transition : CoreTransitionType, context : ContextType]

AuditType ==
    [receipt : PermitType, request : ContextType,
     beforePR : PullRequests \cup {NoPR}, afterPR : PullRequests \cup {NoPR},
     beforeCore : CoreStates, afterCore : CoreStates,
     operation : CoreOperations, outcome : CoreOutcomes]

FollowupTypes ==
    /\ sourceActor \in Actors \cup {NoActor}
    /\ source \in {NoSource} \cup SourceType
    /\ follow \in FollowType
    /\ permit \in {NoPermit} \cup PermitType
    /\ audit \in {NoAudit} \cup AuditType

SourceAuthority == <<source.history.ratified, source.pr, source.decision>>

EligibleSource ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ source.isPlan
    /\ source.owes
    /\ source.history.state = "merged"
    /\ source.history.ratified # NoP
    /\ source.history.proposal = source.history.ratified
    /\ source.history.prLock = source.history.ratified
    /\ source.history.mergedHead = source.history.head
    /\ source.history.mergedHead # NoHead
    /\ source.pr = SourcePR

\* FollowPR denotes the PR identity in the independently verified obligation
\* binding. Other PRs may present the identical branch name and claimed source.
VerifiedAssociation ==
    /\ source.claim = SourceAuthority
    /\ source.candidatePR = FollowPR
    /\ source.candidatePR # source.pr

FollowupActive == follow.pr # NoPR

FollowupMerged == FollowupActive /\ CorePhase(follow.core) = "merged"

FollowupScopeOK ==
    /\ follow.scopeHead = follow.head
    /\ follow.paths \subseteq AllowedFollowupArtifacts
    /\ follow.tied

FollowupChecksOK ==
    /\ follow.ciHead = follow.head
    /\ follow.decisions
    /\ follow.graph
    /\ follow.gate \in {"pass", "skip"}
    /\ (follow.gate = "skip" => FollowupScopeOK)

\* The receipt binds even observations that can change while a core call is
\* outstanding. A fresh head or new scope/check evidence needs fresh acceptance.
FollowContext(a, authenticated) ==
    [authority |-> source.claim, sourcePR |-> source.pr,
     pr |-> source.candidatePR, head |-> follow.head, core |-> follow.core,
     actor |-> a, authenticated |-> authenticated,
     ci |-> <<follow.ciHead, follow.gate, follow.decisions, follow.graph>>,
     scope |-> <<follow.scopeHead, follow.paths, follow.tied>>,
     target |-> follow.target]

FollowupSourceAuthorized == FollowupActive => EligibleSource

FollowupAssociationAuthenticated == FollowupActive => VerifiedAssociation

FollowupSourcePreserved == source # NoSource => SourceHistory = source.history

FollowupStableIdentity ==
    /\ (FollowupActive => follow.pr = source.candidatePR /\ follow.pr # source.pr)
    /\ (audit # NoAudit /\ audit.beforePR # NoPR => audit.afterPR = audit.beforePR)

FollowupNoNewRatification ==
    /\ follow.planRatification = NoP
    /\ follow.projectLock = NoP

FollowupMergedCurrentHead == FollowupMerged => follow.mergedHead = follow.head

FollowupNarrowMerge == FollowupMerged => FollowupScopeOK

FollowupCurrentDecisionChecks == FollowupMerged => FollowupChecksOK

FollowupTrustedBase == FollowupMerged => follow.target \in TrustedBases

FollowupCommandsAuthorized ==
    audit # NoAudit /\ audit.operation \in {"retry", "resume"} =>
        /\ audit.request.actor \in Directors
        /\ audit.request.authenticated

FollowupCoreAccepted ==
    audit # NoAudit =>
        /\ audit.receipt = permit
        /\ audit.receipt.transition \in WorkflowSteps
        /\ audit.receipt.context = audit.request
        /\ audit.beforeCore = audit.receipt.transition[1]
        /\ audit.beforeCore = audit.request.core
        /\ audit.afterCore = audit.receipt.transition[4]
        /\ follow.core = audit.afterCore
        /\ audit.operation = audit.receipt.transition[2]
        /\ audit.outcome = audit.receipt.transition[3]
        /\ follow.outcome = audit.outcome

FollowupHumanHold ==
    /\ (FollowupActive /\ CorePhase(follow.core) = "closed" => CoreHold(follow.core))
    /\ (FollowupMerged => ~CoreHold(follow.core))
    /\ (audit # NoAudit /\ CoreHold(audit.beforeCore) /\ ~CoreHold(audit.afterCore)
           => audit.operation = "resume")

FollowupRetryRenewsAllowance ==
    audit # NoAudit /\ audit.operation = "retry" =>
        /\ CorePhase(audit.beforeCore) = "blocked"
        /\ CoreAllowance(audit.afterCore) # CoreAllowance(audit.beforeCore)
        /\ CoreRepairs(audit.afterCore) = 0

FollowupClosedRetryResumes ==
    audit # NoAudit /\ audit.operation = "resume" =>
        /\ CorePhase(audit.beforeCore) = "closed"
        /\ audit.afterPR = audit.beforePR
        /\ audit.afterPR # NoPR

FollowupTwoRepairsPerAllowance == FollowupActive => CoreRepairs(follow.core) \in 0..2

HumanMergedPlanFollowupMerges ==
    /\ FollowupMerged
    /\ source.history.mergedBy = "other"
    /\ source.history.merger \in Directors

ClosedFollowupResumesSamePR ==
    /\ FollowupActive
    /\ follow.resumed
    /\ CorePhase(follow.core) = "open"
    /\ follow.pr = FollowPR
    /\ ~CoreHold(follow.core)

SkippedProjectGateFollowupMerges == FollowupMerged /\ follow.gate = "skip"

BlockedFollowupGetsNewAllowance == audit # NoAudit /\ audit.operation = "retry"

ClosedFollowupKeepsHold == FollowupActive /\ CorePhase(follow.core) = "closed" /\ CoreHold(follow.core)

AcceptedEffectFailurePreserved == audit # NoAudit /\ audit.operation = "effect" /\ audit.outcome = "failed"


TypeOK ==
    /\ state \in Kinds
    /\ open \subseteq Questions
    /\ proposal \in Locks
    /\ amends \in Locks
    /\ base \in Locks
    /\ ratified \in Locks
    /\ ratifiedBase \in Locks
    /\ head \in Heads \cup {NoHead}
    /\ gate \in [Heads -> {"none", "pending", "pass", "fail"}]
    /\ prLock \in Locks
    /\ scope \in {"one", "many"}
    /\ mergedBy \in {"nobody", "factory", "other"}
    /\ mergedHead \in Heads \cup {NoHead}
    /\ directedBy \in Actors \cup {NoActor}
    /\ stops \in Nat
    /\ failure \in Failures
    /\ rebuiltAfter \in Failures
    /\ FollowupTypes

OnlyDirectorsDirect == directedBy \in Directors \cup {NoActor}

RatifiesCurrentProposal ==
    state \in Building => (ratified # NoP /\ ratified = proposal)

NoOpenQuestionsWhenRatified == state \in Building => open = {}

AmendsHeldLock == state \in Building => ratifiedBase = amends

MergedGatePassed == FactoryMerged => gate[mergedHead] = "pass"

MergedCurrentHead == FactoryMerged => mergedHead = head

MergedOneProject == FactoryMerged => scope = "one"

MergedLockRatified == FactoryMerged => prLock = ratified

StopLimit == stops <= MaxStops

StoppedHasNoPullRequest == failure \in {"stopped", "limit"} => head = NoHead

\* When a ratified proposal waits for its build, nothing is left of an earlier
\* pull request: no head, CI result, lock, scope or merge.
BuildStartsClean ==
    state = "ratified" =>
        /\ head = NoHead
        /\ gate = [h \in Heads |-> "none"]
        /\ prLock = NoP
        /\ scope = "one"
        /\ mergedBy = "nobody"
        /\ mergedHead = NoHead

\* A retry retires a pull request to build its ratified proposal again only
\* after the build failed its own gate in the factory's run, never after CI's
\* gate failed or the pull request couldn't merge.
RebuildsOwnFailures == rebuiltAfter \in {"none", "gate"}

\* Witnesses.
QuestionsAsked == state = "asked"

GotStuck == state = "stuck"

FoundUnsupported == state = "unsupported"

PullRequestFailed == state = "failed"

OthersClosed == state = "closed"

OthersMerged == state = "merged" /\ mergedBy = "other"

FactoryMerges == FactoryMerged

AmendmentMerges == FactoryMerged /\ ratifiedBase # NoP

BuildStopped == state = "failed" /\ failure = "stopped"

BuildRefusedAtLimit == state = "failed" /\ failure = "limit"

OwnGateFailed == state = "failed" /\ failure = "gate" /\ head # NoHead

CannotMerge == state = "failed" /\ failure = "unmergeable"

RebuiltAndMerged == rebuiltAfter = "gate" /\ FactoryMerged

RebuiltAndStopped == rebuiltAfter = "gate" /\ state = "failed" /\ failure = "stopped"

RebuiltFailedAgain == rebuiltAfter = "gate" /\ state = "failed" /\ failure = "gate" /\ head # NoHead


\* The draft model.
OrdinaryInit ==
    /\ state = "none"
    /\ open = {}
    /\ proposal = NoP
    /\ amends = NoP
    /\ base = NoP
    /\ ratified = NoP
    /\ ratifiedBase = NoP
    /\ head = NoHead
    /\ gate = [h \in Heads |-> "none"]
    /\ prLock = NoP
    /\ scope = "one"
    /\ mergedBy = "nobody"
    /\ mergedHead = NoHead
    /\ directedBy = NoActor
    /\ stops = 0
    /\ failure = "none"
    /\ rebuiltAfter = "none"

ResetPR ==
    /\ head' = NoHead
    /\ gate' = [h \in Heads |-> "none"]
    /\ prLock' = NoP
    /\ scope' = "one"
    /\ mergedBy' = "nobody"
    /\ mergedHead' = NoHead

\* A build stopped before it made a pull request.
StoppedBuild == state = "failed" /\ head = NoHead

\* Every draft the factory can post: questions, statements, stuck or unsupported.
Drafts ==
    {[kind |-> "asked", open |-> Q, p |-> NoP] : Q \in (SUBSET Questions) \ {{}}}
    \cup {[kind |-> "proposed", open |-> {}, p |-> p] : p \in Proposals}
    \cup {[kind |-> k, open |-> {}, p |-> NoP] : k \in {"stuck", "unsupported"}}

\* The factory posts draft d: it asks questions, proposes statements against
\* the base branch's current lock, gets stuck, or finds the issue unsupported.
Draft(d) ==
    /\ ResetPR
    /\ ratified' = NoP
    /\ ratifiedBase' = NoP
    /\ failure' = "none"
    /\ rebuiltAfter' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<base, stops>>
    /\ state' = d.kind
    /\ open' = d.open
    /\ proposal' = d.p
    /\ amends' = IF d.kind = "proposed" THEN base ELSE NoP

Solve(a, d) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state \in {"none", "stuck", "unsupported", "closed"} \/ StoppedBuild
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ Draft(d)

Revise(a, d) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state \in {"asked", "proposed", "stuck", "unsupported", "closed"} \/ StoppedBuild
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ Draft(d)

\* Answering the last open question drafts again, as d.
Choose(a, q, d) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state = "asked"
    /\ q \in open
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ IF open = {q}
          THEN Draft(d)
          ELSE /\ open' = open \ {q}
               /\ UNCHANGED <<state, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                              head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead,
                              stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

Ratify(a, p) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state = "proposed"
    /\ open = {}
    /\ p = proposal
    /\ base = amends
    /\ state' = "ratified"
    /\ ratified' = p
    /\ ratifiedBase' = base
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead,
                   stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

Build(h) ==
    /\ state = "ratified"
    /\ stops < MaxStops
    /\ h \in Heads
    /\ state' = "pr_open"
    /\ head' = h
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![h] = "pending"]
    /\ prLock' = ratified
    /\ scope' = "one"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy, stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

\* The build starts, then stops before it makes a pull request.
StopBuild ==
    /\ state = "ratified"
    /\ stops < MaxStops
    /\ state' = "failed"
    /\ stops' = stops + 1
    /\ failure' = "stopped"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy, rebuiltAfter>>

\* Two builds have already stopped partway, so the factory won't start another.
RefuseBuild ==
    /\ state = "ratified"
    /\ stops = MaxStops
    /\ state' = "failed"
    /\ failure' = "limit"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, rebuiltAfter>>

\* The code fails the gate in the factory's own run: it opens a draft pull
\* request and posts that the build failed.
BuildFailsGate(h) ==
    /\ state = "ratified"
    /\ stops < MaxStops
    /\ h \in Heads
    /\ state' = "failed"
    /\ head' = h
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![h] = "pending"]
    /\ prLock' = ratified
    /\ scope' = "one"
    /\ failure' = "gate"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy, stops, rebuiltAfter>>

\* Someone pushes a new head commit to the pull request, with any content.
Push(h, l, s) ==
    /\ state \in {"pr_open", "failed"}
    /\ head # NoHead
    /\ h # head
    /\ head' = h
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![h] = "pending"]
    /\ prLock' = l
    /\ scope' = s
    /\ rebuiltAfter' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy, stops, failure>>

\* CI's gate reports result r on the pull request's current head.
CIGate(r) ==
    /\ state \in {"pr_open", "failed"}
    /\ head # NoHead
    /\ gate[head] = "pending"
    /\ r \in {"pass", "fail"}
    /\ gate' = [gate EXCEPT ![head] = r]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

NoticeFail ==
    /\ state = "pr_open"
    /\ gate[head] = "fail"
    /\ state' = "failed"
    /\ failure' = "ci"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, rebuiltAfter>>

\* CI's gate passed, but the pull request changes more than its one project
\* or its lock isn't the ratified proposal.
NoticeUnmergeable ==
    /\ state = "pr_open"
    /\ gate[head] = "pass"
    /\ (scope # "one" \/ prLock # ratified)
    /\ state' = "failed"
    /\ failure' = "unmergeable"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, rebuiltAfter>>

\* Retry reopens a failed pull request, or builds a stopped build's ratified
\* proposal again with the stop limit reset.
Retry(a) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state = "failed"
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ failure' = "none"
    /\ IF head = NoHead
          THEN state' = "ratified" /\ stops' = 0
          ELSE state' = "pr_open" /\ UNCHANGED stops
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, rebuiltAfter>>

\* Rebuild builds the ratified proposal again after the build failed its own
\* gate in the factory's run and left a draft pull request. The ratification
\* stands; the draft, its head and CI's result there are retired, so none of
\* them stands for the next build, and the stops are counted afresh.
Rebuild(a) ==
    /\ a \in Directors
    /\ state = "failed"
    /\ failure = "gate"
    /\ head # NoHead
    /\ state' = "ratified"
    /\ directedBy' = a
    /\ failure' = "none"
    /\ stops' = 0
    /\ rebuiltAfter' = failure
    /\ ResetPR
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase>>

Merge ==
    /\ state = "pr_open"
    /\ gate[head] = "pass"
    /\ scope = "one"
    /\ prLock = ratified
    /\ state' = "merged"
    /\ mergedBy' = "factory"
    /\ mergedHead' = head
    /\ base' = prLock
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, directedBy, stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>

OthersMerge ==
    /\ state \in {"pr_open", "failed"}
    /\ head # NoHead
    /\ state' = "merged"
    /\ mergedBy' = "other"
    /\ mergedHead' = head
    /\ base' = prLock
    /\ failure' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, directedBy, stops, rebuiltAfter>>

OthersClose ==
    /\ state \in {"pr_open", "failed"}
    /\ head # NoHead
    /\ state' = "closed"
    /\ failure' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, rebuiltAfter>>

\* The base branch's lock changes elsewhere.
BaseMoves(l) ==
    /\ l # base
    /\ base' = l
    /\ rebuiltAfter' = "none"
    /\ UNCHANGED <<state, open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                   head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy,
                   stops, failure>>

Finished == state = "merged" /\ UNCHANGED vars

OrdinaryNext ==
    \/ \E a \in Actors :
        \/ \E d \in Drafts : Solve(a, d) \/ Revise(a, d)
        \/ Retry(a)
        \/ Rebuild(a)
        \/ \E q \in Questions, d \in Drafts : Choose(a, q, d)
        \/ \E p \in Proposals : Ratify(a, p)
    \/ \E h \in Heads : Build(h) \/ BuildFailsGate(h)
    \/ StopBuild
    \/ RefuseBuild
    \/ \E h \in Heads, l \in Locks, s \in {"one", "many"} : Push(h, l, s)
    \/ \E r \in {"pass", "fail"} : CIGate(r)
    \/ NoticeFail
    \/ NoticeUnmergeable
    \/ Merge
    \/ OthersClose
    \/ \E l \in Locks : BaseMoves(l)
    \/ Finished

\* Known bugs.

\* A bot or someone without write access gets the factory to take the issue.
ObeyAnyone ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E a \in Actors \ Directors :
            /\ state \in {"none", "stuck", "unsupported", "closed"}
            /\ state' = "stuck"
            /\ directedBy' = a
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                           head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead,
                           stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* A ratify naming an earlier proposal's hash is accepted.
RatifyEarlier ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E a \in Directors, p \in Proposals \ {proposal} :
            /\ state = "proposed"
            /\ base = amends
            /\ state' = "ratified"
            /\ ratified' = p
            /\ ratifiedBase' = base
            /\ directedBy' = a
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base,
                           head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead,
                           stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* An amendment is ratified after the base branch's lock has moved.
RatifyOverMovedLock ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E a \in Directors :
            /\ state = "proposed"
            /\ state' = "ratified"
            /\ ratified' = proposal
            /\ ratifiedBase' = base
            /\ directedBy' = a
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base,
                           head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead,
                           stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* The factory merges whichever head passed CI, not the current one.
MergeOnAnyPass ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E h \in Heads :
            /\ state = "pr_open"
            /\ gate[h] = "pass"
            /\ scope = "one"
            /\ prLock = ratified
            /\ state' = "merged"
            /\ mergedBy' = "factory"
            /\ mergedHead' = h
            /\ base' = prLock
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                           head, gate, prLock, scope, directedBy, stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* The factory merges without checking the project's lock.
MergeIgnoringLock ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        /\ state = "pr_open"
        /\ gate[head] = "pass"
        /\ scope = "one"
        /\ state' = "merged"
        /\ mergedBy' = "factory"
        /\ mergedHead' = head
        /\ base' = prLock
        /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                       head, gate, prLock, scope, directedBy, stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* The factory starts a third build after two have stopped partway.
StartPastLimit ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        /\ state = "ratified"
        /\ stops = MaxStops
        /\ state' = "failed"
        /\ stops' = stops + 1
        /\ failure' = "stopped"
        /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                       head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead, directedBy, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* The factory merges a draft pull request whose own gate failed, before
\* anyone says retry.
MergeFailedBuild ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        /\ state = "failed"
        /\ head # NoHead
        /\ state' = "merged"
        /\ mergedBy' = "factory"
        /\ mergedHead' = head
        /\ base' = prLock
        /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                       head, gate, prLock, scope, directedBy, stops, failure, rebuiltAfter>>
        )

\* A retry builds a failed build again but keeps its draft's head, CI's
\* result and lock for the next build.
RebuildKeepsDraft ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E a \in Directors :
            /\ state = "failed"
            /\ failure = "gate"
            /\ head # NoHead
            /\ state' = "ratified"
            /\ directedBy' = a
            /\ failure' = "none"
            /\ stops' = 0
            /\ rebuiltAfter' = failure
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase,
                           head, gate, prLock, scope, mergedBy, mergedHead>>
        )

\* A retry builds a pull request that failed CI's gate again, instead of
\* watching it again.
RebuildAfterCI ==
    /\ UNCHANGED followVars
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ (
        \E a \in Directors :
            /\ state = "failed"
            /\ failure \in {"gate", "ci"}
            /\ head # NoHead
            /\ state' = "ratified"
            /\ directedBy' = a
            /\ failure' = "none"
            /\ stops' = 0
            /\ rebuiltAfter' = failure
            /\ ResetPR
            /\ UNCHANGED <<open, proposal, amends, base, ratified, ratifiedBase>>
        )


\* Bounded environment and integration actions. The ordinary actions above
\* retain their existing arguments and meaning for current watcher callers.
FirstHead == CHOOSE h \in Heads : TRUE

OtherHead == CHOOSE h \in Heads : h # FirstHead

FirstPlan == CHOOSE p \in Proposals : TRUE

FirstDecision == CHOOSE d \in Decisions : TRUE

EmptyFollow ==
    [pr |-> NoPR, head |-> NoHead, ciHead |-> NoHead, gate |-> "none",
     decisions |-> FALSE, graph |-> FALSE, scopeHead |-> NoHead,
     paths |-> {}, tied |-> FALSE, target |-> CHOOSE b \in TrustedBases : TRUE,
     core |-> WorkflowInitial, mergedHead |-> NoHead,
     outcome |-> "none", resumed |-> FALSE,
     planRatification |-> NoP, projectLock |-> NoP]

Init ==
    /\ OrdinaryInit
    /\ sourceActor = NoActor
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ follow = EmptyFollow
    /\ permit = NoPermit
    /\ audit = NoAudit

\* Canonical source observations bound this interface check, while the ordinary
\* issue continues to have its original behaviors while no follow-up is active;
\* an ordinary step discards any pending observation or acceptance receipt.
ObserveSource(mode) ==
    /\ source = NoSource
    /\ state \in {"pr_open", "merged"}
    /\ proposal = FirstPlan
    /\ ratified = FirstPlan
    /\ amends = NoP
    /\ ratifiedBase = NoP
    /\ head = FirstHead
    /\ prLock = ratified
    /\ scope = "one"
    /\ stops = 0
    /\ failure = "none"
    /\ rebuiltAfter = "none"
    /\ gate = [h \in Heads |-> IF h = FirstHead THEN "pending" ELSE "none"]
    /\ (state = "merged" => mergedBy = "other" /\ sourceActor \in Directors)
    /\ (state = "pr_open" => sourceActor = NoActor)
    /\ base = IF state = "merged" THEN ratified ELSE NoP
    /\ source' =
        [history |-> SourceHistory, isPlan |-> mode # "not-plan",
         owes |-> mode # "non-owing", pr |-> SourcePR,
         decision |-> FirstDecision,
         claim |-> <<IF mode = "wrong-plan"
                       THEN CHOOSE p \in Proposals : p # ratified
                       ELSE ratified, SourcePR, FirstDecision>>,
         candidatePR |-> IF mode = "forged-pr"
                          THEN CHOOSE p \in PullRequests : p \notin {SourcePR, FollowPR}
                          ELSE FollowPR]
    /\ follow' = [EmptyFollow EXCEPT !.head = FirstHead,
                  !.paths = AllowedFollowupArtifacts, !.tied = TRUE]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, permit, audit>>

OrdinaryStep ==
    /\ ~FollowupActive
    /\ source' = NoSource
    /\ follow' = EmptyFollow
    /\ permit' = NoPermit
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ ((OrdinaryNext /\ UNCHANGED sourceActor)
        \/ (\E a \in Actors : OthersMerge /\ sourceActor' = a))

\* CI and scope are independent observations. A push retains their old revision
\* stamps, making stale evidence visible rather than turning it into a pass.
ObserveFollowupCI(result) ==
    /\ follow.ciHead # follow.head
    /\ CorePhase(follow.core) # "merged"
    /\ follow' = [follow EXCEPT !.ciHead = follow.head, !.gate = result[1],
                  !.decisions = result[2], !.graph = result[3]]
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ UNCHANGED permit

ObserveFollowupScope ==
    /\ follow.scopeHead # follow.head
    /\ CorePhase(follow.core) # "merged"
    /\ follow' = [follow EXCEPT !.scopeHead = follow.head]
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ UNCHANGED permit

PushFollowup(kind) ==
    /\ FollowupActive
    /\ CorePhase(follow.core) # "merged"
    /\ follow.head = FirstHead
    /\ follow' = [follow EXCEPT !.head = OtherHead,
                  !.paths = IF kind = "broad"
                              THEN AllowedFollowupArtifacts \cup {"project-code"}
                              ELSE AllowedFollowupArtifacts,
                  !.tied = kind # "unrelated",
                  !.target = IF kind = "untrusted"
                               THEN CHOOSE b \in BaseRefs \ TrustedBases : TRUE
                               ELSE CHOOSE b \in TrustedBases : TRUE]
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ UNCHANGED permit

\* This is the trusted environment boundary: it delivers the amended Workflow's
\* acceptance for this entire context, not just for the context-free tuple.
\* The tuple table is a bounded overapproximation of possible core outputs.
\* External Workflow acceptance is delivered for an exact request context.
\* The finite relation is an abstract test fixture, not a local classifier.
\* In particular, the protocol never manufactures acceptance from a branch name.
ReceiveWorkflowStep(t, a, authenticated) ==
    /\ permit = NoPermit
    /\ t \in WorkflowSteps
    /\ t[1] = follow.core
    /\ IF t[2] \in {"retry", "resume"}
          THEN a \in Actors
          ELSE a = NoActor /\ ~authenticated
    /\ permit' = [transition |-> t, context |-> FollowContext(a, authenticated)]
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ UNCHANGED follow

DiscardWorkflowReceipt ==
    /\ permit # NoPermit
    /\ permit' = NoPermit
    /\ audit' = NoAudit
    /\ UNCHANGED follow

MatchingWorkflowReceipt ==
    /\ permit # NoPermit
    /\ audit = NoAudit
    /\ permit.transition \in WorkflowSteps
    /\ permit.transition[1] = follow.core
    /\ permit.context = FollowContext(permit.context.actor, permit.context.authenticated)

FollowupStepAuthority ==
    /\ EligibleSource
    /\ VerifiedAssociation
    /\ IF permit.transition[2] = "open"
          THEN ~FollowupActive
          ELSE FollowupActive

FollowupStepPolicy ==
    LET t == permit.transition IN
    /\ CoreRepairs(t[4]) \in 0..2
    /\ (CorePhase(t[4]) = "closed" => CoreHold(t[4]))
    /\ (CoreHold(t[1]) /\ ~CoreHold(t[4]) => t[2] = "resume")
    /\ (t[2] \in {"retry", "resume"} =>
           permit.context.actor \in Directors /\ permit.context.authenticated)
    /\ (t[2] = "retry" =>
           /\ CorePhase(t[1]) = "blocked"
           /\ CoreAllowance(t[4]) # CoreAllowance(t[1])
           /\ CoreRepairs(t[4]) = 0)
    /\ (t[2] = "resume" => CorePhase(t[1]) = "closed" /\ follow.pr # NoPR)
    /\ (CorePhase(t[4]) = "merged" =>
           /\ t[2] = "merge"
           /\ ~CoreHold(t[1])
           /\ ~CoreHold(t[4])
           /\ FollowupScopeOK
           /\ FollowupChecksOK
           /\ follow.target \in TrustedBases)

\* Commit precisely the accepted before/after core state and effect outcome.
\* Outcome names are opaque to protocol policy; a failed effect is not promoted
\* to a successful merge, repair or resume by this adapter.
RecordFollowupStep(t, nextPR, nextMergedHead) ==
    /\ follow' = [follow EXCEPT !.core = t[4], !.pr = nextPR,
                  !.mergedHead = nextMergedHead, !.outcome = t[3],
                  !.resumed = @ \/ (t[2] = "resume" /\ CorePhase(t[4]) = "open")]
    /\ audit' = [receipt |-> permit,
                  request |-> FollowContext(permit.context.actor, permit.context.authenticated),
                  beforePR |-> follow.pr, afterPR |-> nextPR,
                  beforeCore |-> follow.core, afterCore |-> t[4],
                  operation |-> t[2], outcome |-> t[3]]
    /\ UNCHANGED permit

ApplyFollowupStep ==
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ FollowupStepPolicy
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition,
           IF permit.transition[2] = "open" THEN source.candidatePR ELSE follow.pr,
           IF CorePhase(permit.transition[4]) = "merged" THEN follow.head ELSE follow.mergedHead)

FollowupStep ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>
    /\ (\/ \E r \in {<<"pass", TRUE, TRUE>>, <<"skip", TRUE, TRUE>>,
                      <<"fail", TRUE, TRUE>>, <<"pass", FALSE, TRUE>>,
                      <<"skip", TRUE, FALSE>>} : ObserveFollowupCI(r)
        \/ ObserveFollowupScope
        \/ \E k \in {"narrow", "broad", "unrelated", "untrusted"} : PushFollowup(k)
        \/ \E t \in WorkflowSteps, a \in Actors \cup {NoActor}, ok \in BOOLEAN :
                ReceiveWorkflowStep(t, a, ok)
        \/ DiscardWorkflowReceipt
        \/ ApplyFollowupStep)

Wait == UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ OrdinaryStep
    \/ \E mode \in {"eligible", "non-owing", "not-plan", "forged-pr", "wrong-plan"} : ObserveSource(mode)
    \/ FollowupStep
    \/ Wait

\* Counterexamples are local authorization mistakes, not alternate core policy.
FollowupOpenUnmergedSource ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ source.history.state # "merged"
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "open"
    /\ VerifiedAssociation
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, source.candidatePR, NoHead)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupOpenNonOwingSource ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ source.history.state = "merged"
    /\ ~source.owes
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "open"
    /\ VerifiedAssociation
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, source.candidatePR, NoHead)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupOpenForgedAssociation ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ EligibleSource
    /\ ~VerifiedAssociation
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "open"
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, source.candidatePR, NoHead)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupMergeBroaderScope ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "merge"
    /\ follow.scopeHead = follow.head
    /\ ~(follow.paths \subseteq AllowedFollowupArtifacts)
    /\ follow.ciHead = follow.head
    /\ follow.decisions /\ follow.graph /\ follow.gate = "pass"
    /\ follow.target \in TrustedBases
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, follow.head)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupMergeStaleCI ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "merge"
    /\ FollowupScopeOK
    /\ follow.ciHead # follow.head
    /\ follow.decisions /\ follow.graph /\ follow.gate \in {"pass", "skip"}
    /\ follow.target \in TrustedBases
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, follow.head)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupMergeOldHead ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ FollowupStepPolicy
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "merge"
    /\ follow.head = OtherHead
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, FirstHead)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupRetryUnauthorized ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ permit.transition[2] \in {"retry", "resume"}
    /\ ~(permit.context.actor \in Directors /\ permit.context.authenticated)
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, follow.mergedHead)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupApplyStaleAcceptance ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ permit # NoPermit
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "merge"
    /\ permit.transition[1] = follow.core
    /\ permit.context.head # follow.head
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ FollowupStepPolicy
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, follow.head)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupMergeWithoutGraphCheck ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "merge"
    /\ FollowupScopeOK
    /\ follow.ciHead = follow.head
    /\ follow.decisions /\ ~follow.graph /\ follow.gate = "skip"
    /\ follow.target \in TrustedBases
    /\ RecordFollowupStep(permit.transition, follow.pr, follow.head)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<ordinaryVars, sourceActor, source>>

FollowupResumeReplacesPR ==
    /\ source # NoSource
    /\ MatchingWorkflowReceipt
    /\ FollowupStepAuthority
    /\ FollowupStepPolicy
    /\ permit.transition[2] = "resume"

pins.name: Spec
pins.says: The factory starts with no post on the issue, and every step is a Next step.

pins.name: TypeOK
pins.says: The issue's state is always one of the ten kinds of post, and everything else the factory knows has its expected type.

pins.name: OnlyDirectorsDirect
pins.says: Every command the factory acted on came from a person with write access, never from anyone else or from a bot.

pins.name: RatifiesCurrentProposal
pins.says: Whenever something is ratified, built or merged, it is the current proposal.

pins.name: NoOpenQuestionsWhenRatified
pins.says: Nothing is ratified while a question is still open.

pins.name: AmendsHeldLock
pins.says: A proposal is ratified only while the base branch holds the lock it amends.

pins.name: MergedGatePassed
pins.says: When the factory merges, CI's gate passed on the commit it merged.

pins.name: MergedCurrentHead
pins.says: When the factory merges, the commit it merged is the pull request's current head.

pins.name: MergedOneProject
pins.says: When the factory merges, the pull request changes only its one project.

pins.name: MergedLockRatified
pins.says: When the factory merges, the project's lock is exactly the ratified proposal.

pins.name: StopLimit
pins.says: At most two builds of an issue stop partway before a writer says retry.

pins.name: StoppedHasNoPullRequest
pins.says: When a build stops, or the factory refuses to start one, there is no pull request.

pins.name: BuildStartsClean
pins.says: When a ratified proposal waits for its build, nothing is left of an earlier pull request: no head, CI result, lock, scope or merge.

pins.name: RebuildsOwnFailures
pins.says: A retry retires a pull request to build its ratified proposal again only after the build failed its own gate in the factory's run, never after CI's gate failed or the pull request couldn't merge.

pins.name: QuestionsAsked
pins.says: The factory can ask questions.

pins.name: GotStuck
pins.says: The factory can get stuck.

pins.name: FoundUnsupported
pins.says: The factory can find an issue unsupported.

pins.name: PullRequestFailed
pins.says: A pull request can fail CI's gate.

pins.name: OthersClosed
pins.says: Someone else can close the pull request.

pins.name: OthersMerged
pins.says: Someone else can merge the pull request.

pins.name: FactoryMerges
pins.says: The factory can merge its pull request.

pins.name: AmendmentMerges
pins.says: The factory can merge an amendment to an existing lock.

pins.name: BuildStopped
pins.says: A build can stop before it makes a pull request, and the factory posts that it failed.

pins.name: BuildRefusedAtLimit
pins.says: After two builds of an issue stop partway, the factory can refuse to start a third and post that the build failed.

pins.name: OwnGateFailed
pins.says: When the code fails the gate in the factory's own run, the factory can open a draft pull request and post that the build failed.

pins.name: CannotMerge
pins.says: A pull request that passed CI's gate but changes more than its one project or has a lock other than the ratified proposal can fail.

pins.name: RebuiltAndMerged
pins.says: A writer's retry can build a build that failed its own gate again, and the factory can merge the new build's pull request.

pins.name: RebuiltAndStopped
pins.says: After a retry builds a failed build again, the new build can stop before it makes a pull request, and the factory posts that it failed.

pins.name: RebuiltFailedAgain
pins.says: The new build can fail its own gate again and leave another draft pull request, for another retry.

pins.name: ObeyAnyone
pins.says: A bot or someone without write access gets the factory to take the issue.

pins.name: RatifyEarlier
pins.says: A ratify naming an earlier proposal's hash is accepted.

pins.name: RatifyOverMovedLock
pins.says: An amendment is ratified after the base branch's lock has moved.

pins.name: MergeOnAnyPass
pins.says: The factory merges a commit that passed CI even though it is no longer the pull request's head.

pins.name: MergeIgnoringLock
pins.says: The factory merges without checking that the project's lock is the ratified proposal.

pins.name: StartPastLimit
pins.says: The factory starts a third build after two builds of the issue have stopped partway and no writer has said retry.

pins.name: MergeFailedBuild
pins.says: The factory merges a pull request whose build failed, before a writer says retry and CI's gate passes.

pins.name: RebuildKeepsDraft
pins.says: A retry builds a failed build again but keeps its draft's head, CI's result and lock for the next build.

pins.name: RebuildAfterCI
pins.says: A retry builds a pull request that failed CI's gate again, instead of watching it again.

pins.name: FollowupSourceAuthorized
pins.says: A decision follow-up is authorized only by the exact ratified plan in its merged source pull request and the decision that source still owes.

pins.name: FollowupAssociationAuthenticated
pins.says: A follow-up must match the independently verified association between its source obligation and its own pull-request identity, so a claimed source or matching branch cannot authorize another pull request.

pins.name: FollowupSourcePreserved
pins.says: Observing or processing a decision follow-up preserves the source issue’s ratified plan and merged history.

pins.name: FollowupStableIdentity
pins.says: An authorized follow-up keeps its own pull-request identity through every accepted step, including retries and resumes.

pins.name: FollowupNoNewRatification
pins.says: A decision follow-up neither ratifies a new plan nor fabricates a project lock.

pins.name: FollowupMergedCurrentHead
pins.says: When the factory merges a decision follow-up, it merges that follow-up’s current head.

pins.name: FollowupNarrowMerge
pins.says: A follow-up merge requires independently verified scope on its current head containing only decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md changes tied to its source obligation.

pins.name: FollowupCurrentDecisionChecks
pins.says: A follow-up merge requires successful current-head decision checks including the decision graph check, with the project gate either passed or intentionally skipped together with independently verified follow-up scope.

pins.name: FollowupTrustedBase
pins.says: The factory merges a decision follow-up only into a trusted base.

pins.name: FollowupCommandsAuthorized
pins.says: Only an authenticated person with repository write access, never a bot, may request a decision follow-up retry or resume.

pins.name: FollowupCoreAccepted
pins.says: Given an externally supplied acceptance receipt from the amended Workflow for the exact request context, every applied follow-up step preserves that context and its accepted before-state, after-state and effect outcome.

pins.name: FollowupHumanHold
pins.says: A closed follow-up retains its human hold, and only an accepted explicit resume can clear a hold before a merge.

pins.name: FollowupRetryRenewsAllowance
pins.says: An accepted retry of blocked follow-up work renews its repair allowance with no repairs used.

pins.name: FollowupClosedRetryResumes
pins.says: A retry of closed follow-up work is an explicit resume of the same existing pull request.

pins.name: FollowupTwoRepairsPerAllowance
pins.says: The amended Workflow’s repair count for a follow-up’s current allowance stays at most two.

pins.name: HumanMergedPlanFollowupMerges
pins.says: With the corresponding Workflow steps accepted, an eligible plan merged by a person with write access can lead to a follow-up merge.

pins.name: ClosedFollowupResumesSamePR
pins.says: With the corresponding Workflow resume accepted, a closed follow-up can resume under the same pull-request identity.

pins.name: SkippedProjectGateFollowupMerges
pins.says: A follow-up can merge after an intentional project-gate skip when its current decision checks and independent scope verification succeed.

pins.name: BlockedFollowupGetsNewAllowance
pins.says: With the corresponding Workflow retry accepted, a blocked follow-up can receive a renewed repair allowance.

pins.name: ClosedFollowupKeepsHold
pins.says: A follow-up can close while retaining its human hold.

pins.name: AcceptedEffectFailurePreserved
pins.says: The protocol can preserve a failed effect outcome accepted by the amended Workflow.

pins.name: FollowupOpenUnmergedSource
pins.says: The protocol opens a decision follow-up from a source that has not merged.

pins.name: FollowupOpenNonOwingSource
pins.says: The protocol opens a decision follow-up from a merged source that owes no decision.

pins.name: FollowupOpenForgedAssociation
pins.says: The protocol grants follow-up authority to a pull request with a forged source association.

pins.name: FollowupMergeBroaderScope
pins.says: The factory merges a follow-up without independently verifying its narrow scope on the current head.

pins.name: FollowupMergeStaleCI
pins.says: The factory merges a follow-up using successful decision checks from an earlier head.

pins.name: FollowupMergeOldHead
pins.says: The factory merges an earlier follow-up head despite acceptance and checks for the current head.

pins.name: FollowupRetryUnauthorized
pins.says: The protocol accepts a follow-up retry or resume from a bot, a non-writer or an unauthenticated requester.

pins.name: FollowupApplyStaleAcceptance
pins.says: The protocol applies Workflow acceptance for an earlier request context after the follow-up head has changed.

pins.name: FollowupMergeWithoutGraphCheck
pins.says: The factory treats an intentional project-gate skip as permission to merge despite a failed current decision graph check.

pins.name: FollowupResumeReplacesPR
pins.says: The protocol resumes a closed follow-up by replacing its pull request.

pins.name: FollowupChangesEffectOutcome
pins.says: The protocol changes the effect outcome of an accepted Workflow step.

new.name: FollowupSourceAuthorized
new.says: A decision follow-up is authorized only by the exact ratified plan in its merged source pull request and the decision that source still owes.

new.name: FollowupAssociationAuthenticated
new.says: A follow-up must match the independently verified association between its source obligation and its own pull-request identity, so a claimed source or matching branch cannot authorize another pull request.

new.name: FollowupSourcePreserved
new.says: Observing or processing a decision follow-up preserves the source issue’s ratified plan and merged history.

statements.name: FollowupStableIdentity

new.name: FollowupStableIdentity

statements.new_text:
FollowupStableIdentity ==
    /\ (FollowupActive => follow.pr = source.candidatePR /\ follow.pr # source.pr)
    /\ (audit # NoAudit /\ audit.beforePR # NoPR => audit.afterPR = audit.beforePR)

new.name: FollowupNoNewRatification
new.says: A decision follow-up neither ratifies a new plan nor fabricates a project lock.

new.name: FollowupMergedCurrentHead
new.says: When the factory merges a decision follow-up, it merges that follow-up’s current head.

new.name: FollowupNarrowMerge
new.says: A follow-up merge requires independently verified scope on its current head containing only decisions/, SPEC.md and README.md changes tied to its source obligation.

new.name: FollowupCurrentDecisionChecks
new.says: A follow-up merge requires successful current-head decision checks including the decision graph check, with the project gate either passed or intentionally skipped together with independently verified follow-up scope.

new.name: FollowupTrustedBase
new.says: The factory merges a decision follow-up only into a trusted base.

statements.name: FollowupCoreAccepted

new.name: FollowupCoreAccepted
new.says: Given an externally supplied acceptance receipt from the amended Workflow for the exact request context, every applied follow-up step preserves that context and its accepted before-state, after-state and effect outcome.

statements.new_text:
FollowupCoreAccepted ==
    audit # NoAudit =>
        /\ audit.receipt = permit
        /\ audit.receipt.transition \in WorkflowSteps
        /\ audit.receipt.context = audit.request
        /\ audit.beforeCore = audit.receipt.transition[1]
        /\ audit.beforeCore = audit.request.core
        /\ audit.afterCore = audit.receipt.transition[4]
        /\ follow.core = audit.afterCore
        /\ audit.operation = audit.receipt.transition[2]
        /\ audit.outcome = audit.receipt.transition[3]
        /\ follow.outcome = audit.outcome
